analyst_view.overall: Milan (5th, 24 points, four wins in five) host surprise side Frosinone (6th, 20 points), who have one of the league's most productive attacks. Frosinone miss top scorer Raimondo, long-term injured Grillitsch and the suspended Bracaglia (Raimondo and Bracaglia are in the numbers); Terzic, Calvani and Cichella are fit again, so Terzic, the only fit left-back, should start, with Birligea up front. For Milan, Amorim confirmed on Saturday that Tomori and Gabbia are still out (only Gabbia is on the numbers' list) and that Pavlovic is fit enough to be in the squad, though he may not start; Diawara is expected to partner Gila and De Winter, and Amorim said every player back from international duty, Pulisic and Maignan included, is ready. Amorim also admitted Milan create too little and rarely reach the final third, while warning about Frosinone's speed, wing play and transitions. Referee Luca Pairetto (4.9 cards a game) is confirmed and already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already cut a lot for Raimondo's absence (-19% on Frosinone's goals) and raised a little for both sides' recent form. Tomori, not on the numbers' list, is out and Pavlovic is only on the bench or barely fit, so Milan's back line is makeshift against a fast, direct Frosinone side; Amorim's own worry that Milan create little holds the lean back, so only a mild nudge to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners and already raise Frosinone's side for their big recent corner count (+9.5%) while trimming Milan's (-4.4%). Amorim pointed to Frosinone's one-on-one wingers as the threat, which is exactly what drives that corner count, but it is already in the figure, and Milan's low final-third presence is too; I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and already add Pairetto's strict record (+35%; 4.9 a game over 31 games), whose appointment was confirmed on 18 November. It is not a rivalry and no new suspension risk was reported; Frosinone's quick wingers may draw some fouls from a reshuffled Milan defence, but that is not enough to move the figure, so I stay at about 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.3 shots, already lifted heavily for Frosinone's shooting (+24%) and cut for Milan's low recent volume (-5.8%). Amorim said Milan must shoot more but also that he does not want long-range efforts, and nothing in the lineups changes either attack, so I stay at about 33.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, already raised for Frosinone's sharp recent form (+21%). With Tomori out (not counted) and Pavlovic not fully match-fit, Diawara is likely to start, and Amorim himself warned about Frosinone's numbers in the box and transitions, so a small nudge to about 11.1.
